answer: In mechanism design, a bonded participation fee acts like a costly timber barrier that forces every synthetic agent to stake verifiable cryptographic capital before entry. If an agent attempts a sybil attack by flooding the network with fake identities, the resulting forfeiture of collateral will ripple instantly through its connected accounts to confiscate all linked stakes. Consequently, a malicious node faces certain financial ruin rather than profit, transforming the agent economy into a secure grove of strictly honest, self-enforcing best responses.
